Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Austin/San Antonio TX
550 AM CDT Fri Apr 17 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES... 

- Warm and humid conditions continue today, then cooler than
  normal conditions this weekend into early next week after a 
  strong cold front moves through.

- Dry today with rain chances through the weekend into next week
  as an active pattern returns.

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Saturday)
Issued at 1218 AM CDT Fri Apr 17 2026

Dry and mostly cloudy conditions are expected this morning with 
continued south to southeasterly wind over the region. An upper 
level trough deepens and digs into the Central Plains today which 
puts South Central Texas between a surface low to the northwest and 
high pressure to the east. This set-up with allow for breezy 
southerly wind today with gusts to around 25 mph most favored in the 
eastern half of the CWA. We should see some sunshine as well today 
as clouds scatter mid to late morning leaving afternoon highs warm 
in the upper 80s to mid 90s. 

Wind relaxes late tonight as a cold front approaches our area from 
the northwest, which should be right on our doorstep sometime around 
sunrise to mid-morning on Saturday. The front moves across all of 
South Central Texas during the daytime making temperatures tricky 
with cloud cover and rain chances forecast behind the front given 
its gradual slope. Most guidance indicates afternoon temperatures to 
be in the 50s and 60s and did trend colder on Saturday than the NBM. 
Additionally, gusty northerly wind is expected behind the front 
aiding in the cooler temperatures with some guidance indicating 
gusts as high as 40 mph directly behind the front. Rain is mainly 
expected behind the frontal passage due to overrunning but with good 
elevated instability in place we could still see some thunderstorm 
activity which could produce small hail. Overall rain amounts don't 
appear too impressive with LREF guidance showing about a 25 percent 
chance for a half inch of rain across the area through Saturday 
night.

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Saturday night through Thursday)
Issued at 1218 AM CDT Fri Apr 17 2026

Rain chances continue Saturday night but begin to shift south as 
surface high pressure briefly moves over the area Sunday morning 
before moving east Sunday afternoon. This will leave low to medium 
rain chances primarily in the southern and western-most portions of 
the area Sunday during the day, with mainly cool and cloudy 
conditions in store. Breezy north to east wind continues into Sunday 
morning before easing Sunday afternoon and evening. Though mid-level 
ridging builds over the area Sunday, a disturbance within the 
southwesterly flow will likely generate showers and thunderstorms 
west of the area Sunday night which will shift east across our area 
into Tuesday. The cloudy and cooler conditions continue during this 
time, though wind will be lighter than the weekend. 

We'll start to see the return of southeasterly flow Tuesday which 
looks to continue for the rest of the long term period. This will 
bring a day by day warming trend back to the area with highs 
returning into the 80s mid-week. Weak mid-level ridging remains over 
the area mid to late week keeping precipitation chances low, but 
disturbances aloft and a dryline in West Texas keep rain chances non-
zero.

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 543 AM CDT Fri Apr 17 2026

Ceilings not quite as low as we previously thought, but lower
clouds are in the vicinity. We will keep a tempo group in the San
Antonio airports TAFs for lower ceilings for the next couple of
hours. DRT is still VFR. Low clouds should spread over the
airfield soon. All terminals will rebound to VFR by early this
afternoon. Winds will be gusty this afternoon with gusts up to 25
kts likely. Low clouds will reform later tonight. A cold front 
will bring northerly winds around this time Saturday.
